messages:
jake: Opal reporting widespread 401/429s during their 09:10 UTC campaign burst. They’re on a Dedicated pool `opal-prod-1` (currently 2 nodes). Customer says requests started failing ~09:06 and spiked until ~09:25. Attaching quick curl repro from their app logs:

```
POST /v1/generate  HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer <token>
{
  "prompt": "hello"
}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Redwood-Error: queue_full
Retry-After: 5

...then token rotation path returned 401s intermittently:
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
X-Auth-Error: token_not_found
```

jake: TL;DR: auth errors + queue backpressure during burst. Customer worried pool is undersized + autoscaler didn’t react fast enough. Billing alerted for cost spike too.

maria: Thanks Jake. Can you paste the pool autoscale policy + current instance type? Also did they have scheduled warmup? @raj FYI.

jake: Policy: `min=1, max=6, scale_step=1, cooldown=300s, metric=qps_per_node`
Instance type: `gpu-a100-80gb` (we confirmed). No warmup configured; they were running a TTL token rotation job at campaign start per their app logs (possible auth storm).

raj: Looking at autoscaler logs for opal-prod-1 around 2054321500-2054323000: scaler attempted to scale from 2->3 at 09:08 but cooldown prevented further steps until 09:13. Meanwhile queue depth spiked to ~12k requests. Device-level throughput topped at ~280 qps per GPU (saturated).

raj: Immediate hypothesis: combined auth-retries + sudden QPS spike caused queue thrash and triggered queue_full 429s before scaler could add enough capacity. Token rotation produced a short burst of auth failures that amplified retries.

sara: From Opal’s telemetry (they shared metrics): baseline QPS ~140 sustained, typical 95th ~650, campaign peak observed ~1800 qps for ~10 minutes. Error breakdown: 60% 429 queue_full, 30% 500 gateway (timeouts), 10% 401 auth. CPU/GPU memory usage shows GPUs saturated during peak; queue_time p50 jumped from 20ms -> 1200ms.

maria: Ok. Short-term mitigations we should propose now: 1) bump pool to 6 nodes immediately, 2) temporarily disable strict cooldown or set to 60s, 3) increase queue limit and enable short-lived token caching at ingress to reduce auth backpressure, 4) ask Opal to postpone token rotation for 15m. Who can execute 1+2? @raj

raj: I can run the pool update now. Command I’ll use: `redwoodctl pool update --name opal-prod-1 --min 4 --max 12 --autoscale-cooldown 60` then `redwoodctl scale --name opal-prod-1 --replicas 6 --priority emergency`.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INCIDENT-OPAL-205432 (priority P2) — responders: @raj, @maria, @jake.

lynn_finance: Opal’s billing alert flagged a +3x cost spike. Finance can flag emergency credit while we triage, but we need an RCA and cost mitigation plan. Noted.

jake: I told Opal to pause token rotation and to hold back the last tranche of the campaign for 20m. They approved. I also shared the temporary increase and asked for app-level retry jitter.

raj: Update: pool scaled to 6 replicas at 09:18 UTC; queue depth dropped from 12k -> 800 within ~70s; 429 rate dropped to <1% after 90s. Auth 401s persisted at low rate until they rolled back token rotation at 09:22. Post-mortem looks actionable.

maria: Good recovery. For long-term right-sizing + prevention: we should recommend Opal reserve capacity to cover scheduled campaigns. Proposal: set reserved capacity to handle campaign peak 1800 qps with 60% target utilization. Using measured per-GPU sustained throughput ~300 qps at 100%, at 60% usable = 180 qps/node -> required nodes = ceil(1800/180)=10 nodes. Recommend reserved pool = 10 nodes with max burst to 15. Also: schedule warmup 15m before campaign to pre-populate KV cache and avoid cold-path jitter.

sara: Additional recommendations: - implement client-side exponential backoff with jitter - add auth token prefetching and short-lived caching at edge - add a canary ramp job (simulate 5% of the campaign traffic 30m prior).

raj: Action items & owners: - Short-term scale + cooldown change: raj (done) - Ask customer to pause token rotation & add jitter: jake (in progress) - Approve emergency credit: lynn_finance (ack) - Schedule warmup + reserved capacity proposal: maria + raj, target PR by EOD tomorrow.

maria: For the reserved capacity PR include: exact node type choice, cost estimate, autoscale guardrails (burst window, cooldown tweaks), and a warmup runbook with commands: `redwoodctl pool warmup --name opal-prod-1 --duration 900 --simulate-qps 200`

jake: Opal asked for an ETA on the RCA. I’ll draft a short incident summary and timeline and include the kernel metrics + autoscaler logs. Will circulate to them and to finance for credits.

sara: One more note — we should consider a platform change: allow scheduled pre-scale windows for customers (manual or cron) that temporarily raise min replicas without touching max. This would prevent cooldown-related undershoot for predictable spikes. I'll spin up a feature ticket.

maria: Agreed. Thanks team. If anyone sees regression or Opal re-run campaign early, escalate to oncall immediately.

jake: Closing loop with Opal now. Will post RCA draft here when ready. :white_check_mark:
